newsitem.title: POLAND: Parliament body blames Polish security over Oleksy.
newsitem.headline: Parliament body blames Polish security over Oleksy.

text.p: A special parliamentary committee said on Wednesday that Polish UOP security officers had acted illegally in bringing spy allegations that led prime minister Jozef Oleksy to quit in January, television news said.
The committee is dominated by politicians aligned with the ex-communist Oleksy, who denies the allegations that he informed for Soviet and Russian intelligence.
Polish public television said opposition party members of the committee dissented from the report, which found that UOP officers may have committed crimes while gathering evidence.

The television quoted the committee's chiefs as saying its final report was backed by seven members from the ruling leftist coalition, while three opposition politicians voted against and one abstained.
Opposition members, in minority resolutions, said the UOP officers had not broken the law.

The so-called Oleksy affair erupted in December, when the then interior minister Andrzej Milczanowski told a stunned parliament that the security service had evidence Oleksy had in the past passed information to Moscow intelligence.
Oleksy, while proclaiming his innocence, quit after prosecutors decided to probe the allegations and he now heads the social democrats -- senior party in the ruling coalition.
Prosecutors later dropped their investigation, saying the UOP evidence was flawed and inadequate.

Oleksy and his supporters have said the allegations were cooked up by UOP officers sympathetic to former Solidarity leader Lech Walesa, who in December was just about to hand over Poland's presidency to Oleksy's fellow ex-communist Aleksander Kwasniewski after losing elections.
The committee report did not contain a recommendation that Milczanowski be tried, although it did say he might bear "personal responsibility," PAP news agency reported.
